# How do I download generated files from Text to Speech?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/how-do-i-download-generated-files-from-text-to-speech.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How do I download generated files from Text to Speech?

You can download the generated files in two ways:

You can download a generated file immediately by clicking the download button on the bottom right after generating the content.

Previously generated files can be downloaded from your history. 

To access your history, log in to your account and select "Text to Speech" in the sidebar, then access your history by clicking the history tab in the panel on the right side of the screen. On narrow screens, you can access your history by clicking the history icon above the "Generate speech" button.

From your history, you can click the download icon to see the option to download as either an MP3 (128kbps) or WAV file. 

You can also click <strong>Advanced</strong> to download in additional file formats:

* MP3 (192kbps)
* MP3 (256kbps)
* M4A
* FLAC

# How do I select the language and accent?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/how-do-i-select-the-language-and-accent.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How do I select the language and accent?

<strong>
  Language when generating via the website
</strong>

When you generate audio on the ElevenLabs website, our AI automatically detects the language based on the context of the text of your prompt. This means that it's best to avoid using multiple languages in a single prompt, as this can cause confusion about which language should be used. At the moment, it isn’t possible to specify a language when generating on the website. 

 

<strong>
  Language when generating via API
</strong>

If you generate audio through the API, you can manually specify the language of your prompt using the `language_code` parameter. This is an optional parameter that accepts ISO 639-1 language codes. 

This can be useful for short or ambiguous prompts, such as when the text includes only numbers. Specifying the language ensures the normalizer applies the correct rules for that language.

For more information on normalization, see [this article. ](/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/why-are-numbers-dates-symbols-and-acronyms-not-properly-pronounced-or-spoken-in-the-correct-language)

 

<strong>
  Accent
</strong>

The accent that is used for your generation comes from the voice you're using. If you use a voice that hasn’t been trained on the language you’re generating, you may notice a slight accent from the voice’s original language.

For the best results, we recommend using a voice that has been trained on audio in the language you’re generating, with your preferred accent. This helps the AI understand pronunciation and intonation more accurately.

This is especially important for languages that are similar or share many common words. Choosing a voice trained on the correct language ensures that the AI uses the correct pronunciation and accent.

You can:

* <strong>Create a cloned voice</strong> using audio in your preferred language and accent.
* <strong>Browse the Voice Library</strong> and use the search filters to find suitable voices that
  match your needs.

<img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/40034290968081" alt="" />

# How can I force a certain pronunciation of a word or name?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/how-can-i-force-a-certain-pronunciation-of-a-word-or-name.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How can I force a certain pronunciation of a word or name?

If you want to force a certain pronunciation, you can use SSML phoneme tags. We support both IPA and CMU. However, we have found that CMU, with the current implementation, seems to be a bit more predictable, consistent, and better overall. You can find out more about this in our [guide to Prompting.](/docs/overview/capabilities/text-to-speech/best-practices#prompting-eleven-v3)

This is available on the following models:

* English v1
* Turbo v2
* Flash v2

Alternatively, a workaround is to find an alternative spelling and write a word more phonetically. You can employ various tricks such as capital letters, dashes, apostrophes, or even single quotation marks around a single letter or letters.

As an example, a word like "trapezii" could be spelt "trapezIi" to put more emphasis on the "ii" of the word.

# How can I add pauses?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/how-can-i-add-pauses.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How can I add pauses?

There are a few ways to introduce a pause or break and influence the rhythm and cadence of the speaker. The most consistent way is programmatically using the syntax `<break time="1.5s" />`. This will create an exact and natural pause in the speech. It is not just added silence between words, but the AI has an actual understanding of this syntax and will add a natural pause.

However, since this is more than just inserted silence, how the AI handles these pauses can vary. As usual, the voice used plays a pivotal role in the output. Some voices, those trained with a few "uh"s and "ah"s in them, have shown to sometimes insert those vocal mannerisms during the pauses, like a real speaker might.

An example could look like this:

"Give me one second to think about it." `<break time="1.0s" />` "Yes, that would work."

Break time should be described in seconds, and the AI can handle pauses of up to 3 seconds in length and can be used in Speech Synthesis and via the API.

There is one caveat when using SSML breaks; if you use an excessive amount in your text, it might cause issues. The speech of the AI might start speeding up and become very fast, or it might introduce more noise in the audio and a few other strange artifacts. We are working on resolving this.

<strong>
  Alternatives
</strong>

These options are inconsistent and might not always work. We recommend using the syntax above for consistency.

One trick that seems to provide the most consistent output - sans the above option - is a simple dash `-` or the em-dash `—`. You can even add multiple dashes such as `-- --` for a longer pause.

"It - is - getting late."

Ellipsis `...` can sometimes also work to add a pause between words but usually also adds some "hesitation" or "nervousness" to the voice that might not always fit.

I... yeah, I guess so..."

# Is there a way to preview audio without losing quota before downloading?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/is-there-a-way-to-preview-audio-without-losing-quota-before-downloading.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# Is there a way to preview audio without losing quota before downloading?

Unfortunately, at this time, we do not offer download-based deduction as an alternative to generation-based deduction. There is currently no way to preview generations without deducting quota.

When you press 'Generate' on the website, you will be deducted credits since the servers need to spin up and the audio needs to be generated.  There's no way to test or preview a voice using your own text without using credits.

We do permit two free regenerations in Speech Synthesis via the website in the following circumstances:

* The prompt (for text-to-speech) or file (for speech-to-speech), voice and model remain the same.  You can change the voice setting sliders.
* The first generation was made less than two hours ago.
* You haven't refreshed the page since generating the original audio.

If this is the case, you will see 'Regenerate speech', and the number of free regenerations remaining will be displayed if you hover over the 'Regenerate speech' button:

<img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/28015504910609" alt="" />

 

Once your free regenerations have been used, the button will return to 'Generate speech', and the number of credits that will be used for the generation will be displayed:

<img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/28015488674961" alt="" />

 

Free regenerations are only available in Speech Synthesis via the website.  They are not available via the API.

We are looking into whether there's a way for us to facilitate previews at this quality without raising prices or costs. We are also exploring ways to make the AI more controllable, so you don't have to preview and instead get the desired result, hopefully on the first try.

# How to produce emotions?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/how-to-produce-emotions.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How to produce emotions?

The model is sensitive to the wider situation surrounding each utterance - it assesses whether something makes sense by how it ties to preceding and succeeding text. This zoomed-out perspective allows it to intonate longer fragments properly by overlaying a particular train of thought stretching multiple sentences with a unifying emotional pattern.

There are a couple of tips for producing emotions: 

Context is key for generating specific emotions. Thus, if one inputs laughing/funny text they
might get a happy output. Similarly with anger, sadness, and other emotions, setting the context
is key. 

Punctuation and voice settings play the leading role in how the output is delivered. 

Add emphasis by putting the relevant words/phrases in quotation marks.

For speech generated using a cloned voice, the speaking style contained in the samples you
upload for cloning is replicated in the output. So if the speech in the uploaded sample is
monotone, the model will struggle to produce expressive output. 

These are the best tips for producing emotions but do not guarantee the result. We will be introducing features that will allow for the control of emotions within the text.

# What is Eleven v3?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/what-is-eleven-v3-alpha.md

# What is Eleven v3?

Eleven v3 is our latest and most expressive Text to Speech model, offering:

* More human-like generations with higher quality overall

* Support for audio tags

* emotions: \[sad] \[angry] \[happily]

* delivery direction: \[whispers] \[shouts]

* non-verbal reactions: \[laughs]\[clears throat] \[sighs]

* Dialogue mode to support natural sounding audio with multiple speakers

* Support for 70+ languages

It can produce breathtaking output, but its more variable consistency and higher latency mean it’s not suitable for real-time or conversational use cases. For those, we recommend the v2/v2.5 Turbo or Flash models. We’re working on a real-time version of Eleven v3.

You can generate using v3 via API using our [Create speech](/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert) and [Stream speech](/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/stream) endpoints by specifying model ID `eleven_v3`.

You can also use our [Create dialogue](/docs/api-reference/text-to-dialogue/convert) and [Stream dialogue ](/docs/api-reference/text-to-dialogue/stream)endpoints to create a natural sounding dialogue with multiple speakers.

Visit the following resources for more information:

# What's the maximum amount of characters and text I can generate?

# What's the maximum amount of characters and text I can generate?

In [Speech Synthesis](/docs/speech-synthesis/), using the website, you can generate up to 5,000 characters in a single generation on any paid plan and up to 2,500 on all free plans.

However, if you plan on generating longer-form content of more than a few thousand characters, we highly recommend using [Studio](/docs/projects) (previously Projects) which allows you to generate extremely long-form content such as books and novels very easily. You can read more about it [here](/docs/projects).

 

If you're generating using the API, the maximum length of input varies depending on which model you're using:

<strong>
  Text-to-speech
</strong>

Flash v2.5 - up to 40,000 characters (\~40 minutes of audio)

Turbo v2.5 - up to 40,000 characters (\~40 minutes of audio)

Flash v2 - up to 30,000 characters (\~30 minutes of audio)

Turbo v2 - up to 30,000 characters (\~30 minutes of audio)

Multilingual v1 and v2 - up to 10,000 characters (\~10 minutes of audio)

English v1 and v2 - up to 10,000 characters (\~10 minutes of audio)

<strong>
  Speech-to-speech
</strong>

Multilingual v2 - up to 10 minutes of audio

English v2 - up to 5 minutes of audio

# What languages can the AI speak?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/what-languages-can-the-ai-speak.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# What languages can the AI speak?

Any voice can speak any language currently supported by the AI; however, if you do not use a voice that is native to the language you want the AI to speak, for example, you use a generated voice or a voice cloned speaking English, the AI might have a slight English accent or might drift in and out of similar languages.

For a full list of all supported languages, please see this article: [What languages do you support?](/docs/help-center/other/what-languages-do-you-support)

The way the current model works is that you don't select a specific language. Instead, you write in the language you want the AI to speak, and the AI understands automatically. However, since there can be some overlap between different languages where they use similar words and vocabulary but with quite different pronunciations and accents, you should use a cloned voice that was cloned speaking the language with the correct accent as this will ensure the AI has the most context for how to speak something and in what language.

<strong>
  The language is determined by the text, while the accent and pronunciation are determined by the
  voice itself.
</strong>

We are looking into developing new technology to facilitate the selection of language, but the way the AI is built means that all of this is still in progress.

# Why is my voice mispronouncing certain words?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/why-is-my-voice-mispronouncing-certain-words.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# Why is my voice mispronouncing certain words?

Mispronunciations can happen for a few different reasons. The most common one is that the word is just misspelled. The AI will not try to correct any words that are misspelled, and it will try to read them exactly as they are written. So it's important to double-check and make sure that the text is proofread and finished before having the AI read it.

If you want to force a certain pronunciation, you can use SSML phoneme tags with our English V1 and Turbo V2 models. You can find out more about this in our [guide to Prompting.](/docs/best-practices/prompting/controls#pronunciation)  

Sometimes, the AI might mispronounce words or have a strange accent that is not the one you are expecting. This can happen for a few reasons, and in most cases, it's very voice-dependent and language-dependent. The best way to ensure the correct accent and pronunciation is to clone a voice with the correct accent and pronunciation. This will give the AI the most context when generating the voiceover.

The language is specified by the text, and the accent is specified by the voice. So if you're writing in a language that might share a lot of common words or is fairly closely related to another language, the AI might have a hard time understanding how to pronounce certain words or switch between accents.

However, under certain circumstances, the AI might mispronounce words that are written correctly, even in English. This seems to be highly dependent on the voice used and the text used, but should be a rare occurrence.

# Why are numbers, dates, symbols and acronyms not properly pronounced or spoken in the correct language?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/why-are-numbers-dates-symbols-and-acronyms-not-properly-pronounced-or-spoken-in-the-correct-language.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# Why are numbers, dates, symbols and acronyms not properly pronounced or spoken in the correct language?

Numbers, dates, symbols and acronyms can present a challenge to the AI, as there are often multiple ways that they could be delivered correctly. This can also depend on the language that is being used, for example, “11” could be read as "Eleven," but it could also be "Once" in Spanish or "Elf" in German.  

There are several ways you can ensure the correct delivery of numbers, dates, acronyms and symbols.

 

<strong>
  Write out fully, in words
</strong>

For the best results, we recommend writing numbers, acronyms, dates and symbols fully, in words, in the way that you would like the AI to deliver them. This ensures that the AI has the most context so that it will provide the correct output. For example, for “\$100”, we would recommend writing either "a hundred dollars" or "one hundred dollars" to ensure you get the result you would like.  

 

<strong>
  Using an LLM
</strong>

If you are using a large language model to generate your text prompts, for example, when using [ElevenAgents](/docs/conversational-ai/overview), you can prompt the model to always write numbers, dates, symbols, and acronyms out in words in whichever way you would prefer them to be delivered by the AI.

 

<strong>
  Normalization
</strong>

If you’re generating via the API, you can specify whether to apply text normalization using the `apply_text_normalization` parameter. Text normalization spells out numbers and dates to ensure better pronunciation  This option does add latency as the normalization process takes additional processing time.

The`apply_text_normalization` parameter has three modes:

* on, which means it is always applied
* off, which means it is never applied
* auto, which means that the AI will automatically decide when to apply text normalization

You can also specify the language of your prompt using the `language_code`parameter. This is an optional parameter that accepts ISO 639-1 language codes. 

This can be useful for short or ambiguous prompts, such as when the text includes only numbers or symbols. Specifying the language ensures the normalizer applies the correct rules for that language.

For more information, see our <a href="/docs/api-reference/introduction">API reference.</a>

Normalization is enabled by default when generating using Text to Speech via the website.  

In Studio, the default is for normalization to be automatically applied, meaning that the AI will decide when to apply text normalization. You can also set normalization to be always applied - this option is in <strong>Project settings</strong> under the <strong>Advanced</strong> tab.

# Can I connect a non-Twilio phone to ElevenAgents?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/conversational-agents/eleven-labs-agents-formerly-conversational-ai/can-i-connect-a-non-twilio-phone-to-eleven-agents.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# Can I connect a non-Twilio phone to ElevenAgents?

Yes — you can connect non-Twilio numbers using SIP trunking.

SIP trunking allows you to establish a direct connection between your telephony infrastructure and the ElevenAgents platform. This means you can route inbound calls from any supported phone number — even if it's not hosted on Twilio — to your agents.

Using SIP trunking, you're not limited to Twilio numbers and can integrate with existing carriers or on-premise systems. 

For more information on the setup of SIP trunking, please see our [ElevenAgents documentation.](/docs/agents-platform/phone-numbers/sip-trunking)

# How many ElevenAgents requests can I make and can I increase it?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/conversational-agents/eleven-labs-agents-formerly-conversational-ai/how-many-eleven-agents-requests-can-i-make-and-can-i-increase-it.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How many ElevenAgents requests can I make and can I increase it?

The concurrency limit (concurrent calls/conversations running in parallel) depends on your subscription.

Below are the current rates at the time of writing this per workspace (including all of your agents), but please note that we will likely revisit them in the future.

* Free: 4
* Starter: 6
* Creator: 10
* Pro: 20
* Scale: 30
* Business: 30

If you require a higher number of concurrent requests, please reach out to our Enterprise Department directly via [this webpage](https://elevenlabs.io/enterprise). We will be happy to discuss a tailor-made plan that meets your specific requirements.

You can also enable burst pricing for individual agents, which allows you to temporarily exceed your concurrency limit during high-demand periods. When enabled, your agents can handle up to 3 times your normal concurrency limit, with excess calls charged at double the standard rate. For more information, see our [documentation](/docs/agents-platform/guides/burst-pricing).

# Can I connect Twilio to ElevenAgents?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/conversational-agents/eleven-labs-agents-formerly-conversational-ai/can-i-connect-twilio-to-eleven-agents.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# Can I connect Twilio to ElevenAgents?

Yes — we offer full integration with Twilio for ElevenAgents.

Twilio makes it easy to handle both inbound and outbound calls through ElevenAgents. All you need is a paid Twilio account and an active Twilio phone number.

To get started:

Import your Twilio number into the platform.

Verify the number using your Twilio SID and Auth Token, available in the Twilio admin console.

Once verified, you can assign the number to a specific agent to handle incoming or outgoing
calls.

This setup allows your agent to seamlessly manage calls using your existing Twilio infrastructure.

For more information, please see our [ElevenAgents documentation.](/docs/agents-platform/phone-numbers/twilio-integration/native-integration)

# How do I share an agent with a Basic Seat member of my workspace?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/conversational-agents/eleven-labs-agents-formerly-conversational-ai/how-do-i-share-an-agent-with-a-basic-seat-member-of-my-workspace.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How do I share an agent with a Basic Seat member of my workspace?

Users on Basic seats have full access to ElevenAgents and can access and edit agents in your workspace that have been shared with them.<br /> <br />To invite additional Basic Seat members to your workspace:

Click your profile icon in the top right corner of the website to open your account menu.

Select <strong>Workspace settings</strong>

Go to the [Members](https://elevenlabs.io/app/workspace/members) tab

Click <strong>Invite New User</strong>

Enter the email address of the person you want to invite

<img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/45371405017105" alt="" />

Once the new member has joined your workspace, you'll need to make sure that the agent is shared so that they can access it. 

Go to your [Agents page](https://elevenlabs.io/app/agents/agents) and find the agent you want to
share

Click the <strong>More actions</strong> (three dots) button

Select <strong>Share agent</strong>

In the sharing settings, you can either share directly by searching for the specific user, or
you can set <strong>Workspace Access</strong> to <strong>Admin</strong> - this means that
everyone in the workspace will be able to edit the agent.

You'll also need to share any resources the agent relies on, such as voices or pronunciation
dictionaries.

# How much does ElevenAgents cost?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/conversational-agents/eleven-labs-agents-formerly-conversational-ai/how-much-does-eleven-agents-cost.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How much does ElevenAgents cost?

There is no cost to create your agent. The cost of calls depends on whether your agent is voice only, multimodal or text only. 

You need to have purchased Pay As You Go credits, or enabled usage based billing (only available on legacy subscriptions), before you can exceed your credit quota. You can find out more about these options here: 

* [What is usage based billing?](/docs/help-center/account/general/what-is-usage-based-billing)
* [Pay As You Go](/docs/overview/administration/pay-as-you-go)

 

<strong>
  Voice only
</strong>

Voice only calls are charged based on the call duration, with a 95% discount for periods of silence longer than 10 seconds. 

For details of how many minutes are included with each subscription plan, see our [ElevenAgents pricing.](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/agents) 

The length of the call is measured based on the connection duration. This includes the time from when you begin the call, to when you end the call or the window is closed. This is why the call itself may be shorter than the duration you are charged for.

 

<strong>
  Multimodal
</strong>

Multimodal calls are charged based on the call duration, with a 95% discount for periods of silence longer than 10 seconds. You're also charged for each text message - for costs, see the table below. LLM costs are passed through separately - for more information, see the following <strong>LLM costs</strong> section.

 

<strong>
  Text only
</strong>

In text only calls you're charged for each text message - for costs, see [ElevenAgents pricing.](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/agents) LLM costs are passed through separately - for more information, see the following <strong>LLM costs</strong> section.

 

<strong>
  LLM costs
</strong>

LLM costs are passed through separately - you can access estimated costs for each agent, based on its past behaviour and knowledge base, from the <strong>Detailed costs</strong> button in the <strong>Primary LLM</strong> selector in your agents settings. 

<img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/45943142315153" alt="" />

 

For more information on how to start creating your voice agent, please see our [ElevenAgents documentation.](/docs/agents-platform/overview)

# What can I create with ElevenAgents?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/conversational-agents/eleven-labs-agents-formerly-conversational-ai/what-can-i-create-with-eleven-agents.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# What can I create with ElevenAgents?

You can create fully customized and interactive voice agents. 

You can customize the voice, the first message and the system prompt for your agent. The system prompt will inform your agent’s behavior, style, and demeanor.  

You can also choose the LLM your agent uses. We offer ElevenLabs hosted LLMs for ultra-low latency and reduced reasoning cost. You can also chose from the leading models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, or use your own custom LLM.

You can also create your own knowledge base. This is additional information you can provide your agent on top of the base understanding of the LLM you selected. Non-enterprise users are limited up to 20MB in total. 

RAG allows you to add more information to your agent's knowledge base. RAG cannot be enabled for documents smaller than 500 bytes. When RAG is enabled, the size of knowledge base items that can be assigned to an agent is increased. The total limit is dependent on your subscription plan - see our [Agents documentation](/docs/agents-platform/customization/knowledge-base/rag#usage-limits) for details. 

For more information on how to start creating your voice agent, please see our [ElevenAgents documentation.](/docs/agents-platform/overview)

# What is ElevenAgents?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/conversational-agents/eleven-labs-agents-formerly-conversational-ai/what-is-eleven-agents.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# What is ElevenAgents?

ElevenAgents is a platform for deploying customized, interactive voice agents. Our ElevenAgents orchestration platform combines

* Speech to Text (the ears)
* LLM (the brain)
* Text to Speech (the voice)

along with built in interruption handling, turn taking logic, and knowledge bases. Altogether, our platform makes it easy to create interactive agents that you and your users can talk to like a person.

For more information on ElevenAgents, please see our [documentation](/docs/agents-platform/overview). 

We also have a series of YouTube videos and tutorials covering ElevenAgents. You can visit [our YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@elevenlabsio) to access these.

# How do I use tools with ElevenAgents?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/conversational-agents/eleven-labs-agents-formerly-conversational-ai/how-do-i-use-tools-with-eleven-agents.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How do I use tools with ElevenAgents?

You can connect <strong>Client Tools</strong>, <strong>Webhooks</strong>, or <strong>System Tools</strong> to your agent to enhance its functionality.

<strong>Tools</strong> allow your agent to interact with external data, systems, and the environment
it's running in. You define which tools your agent can use, and it will automatically choose the
appropriate one during a conversation.

<strong>Webhooks</strong> are tools that connect your assistant to external APIs. They’re ideal for
tasks like:

* Booking meetings
* Accessing or updating databases
* Telling the current time
* And much more

This type of tool enables powerful real-time interactions with your services.

<strong>Client Tools</strong> interact directly with the user's browser or device where the agent is
hosted. They’re typically used to:

* Redirect users within your site
* Send on-screen notifications
* Guide users through website flows

These tools help deliver a more integrated and seamless user experience.

<strong>System Tools</strong> are built-in and ready to use as soon as your agent is created. They
handle essential conversation management tasks like:

* Ending a call
* Transferring a call
* Switching languages

These foundational tools ensure your agent can manage core interactions out of the box.

For more information on tool implementation, please see our [ElevenAgents documentation.](/docs/agents-platform/customization/tools)

# Where can I locate the reason for my call failing?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/conversational-agents/eleven-labs-agents-formerly-conversational-ai/where-can-i-locate-the-reason-for-my-call-failing.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# Where can I locate the reason for my call failing?

You can find all failed (and successful) calls on the Call History page.

Failed calls will display a red error message that explains why the call ended early or didn’t connect at all.

Here are a few common errors you might see:

* <strong>
    Host elevenlabs.io is not allowed to connect to this agent
  </strong>
  <br />
  This error usually occurs when the agent has an allowlist enabled, but the caller is using a
  shared link. Removing the allowlist will resolve this issue.
* <strong>
    Missing required dynamic variables in \_\_\_\_\_\_ : \{‘dynamic variable name’}
  </strong>
  <br />
  This error typically appears when no transcript or call is generated. It means the caller didn’t
  configure a required dynamic variable correctly.
* <strong>
    Agent has exceeded its daily call limit of
  </strong>
  <br />
  The agent has a preset daily call limit. This error indicates that the call failed because the
  limit was exceeded.
* <strong>Override is not allowed for this AI agent</strong>
  <br />A simple error message indicating an attempt was made to override the prompt or other
  settings, but the override feature wasn’t enabled.
* <strong>
    Missing dynamic variable after agent transfer
  </strong>
  <br />
  This means a dynamic variable required by the transferred-to agent wasn’t available, causing the
  call to end.

If your call failed and no error message is displayed, please contact support by emailing us at [team@elevenlabs.io](mailto:team@elevenlabs.io).

# Which voices in the voice library are native to a specific language?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/speech-synthesis/text-to-speech/which-voices-in-the-voice-library-are-native-to-a-specific-language.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# Which voices in the voice library are native to a specific language?

All pre-made voices and generated voices are English. This means that they might not have the correct accent or pronunciation when speaking other languages.

In the voice library, under the professional category, you can find voices that the community has shared with us. These voices are their own [Professional Voice Clones](/docs/product-guides/voices/voice-cloning/professional-voice-cloning) of their voices. These voices generally have a language tag that indicates the language in which they were cloned, making them native to that language.  You can also use the language search filter to filter for specific languages.

# What is Audio Native?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/audio-native/what-is-audio-native.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# What is Audio Native?

Audio Native is an embedded audio player that automatically voices content of a web page using ElevenLab’s text-to-speech service. It can also be used to embed pre-generated content from a Studio project into a web page. All it takes to deploy on your site is a brief snippet of html. In addition, Audio Native comes with built-in metrics so you can track audience engagement through a listener dashboard.

Audio Native is available on the Creator plan and above.

For more details, please see our <a href="/docs/creative-platform/audio-tools/audio-native">Audio Native overview.</a>

# How to Update an Audio Native Player

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/audio-native/how-to-update-an-audio-native-player.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How to Update an Audio Native Player

Made edits to your website or decided to use a new voice? Here’s how to update your Audio Native player to reflect those changes:

<strong>Open the Studio project</strong><br />Go to the [Audio Native page](https://elevenlabs.io/app/audio-native), click the three dots next to the page you'd like to update, and select <strong>Edit Audio</strong>. This will open the corresponding Studio project.<br />

<img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/34478880523025" alt="" />

<strong>Make your changes</strong><br />Update your project as needed, such as changing the voice or editing the script.

<strong>Export the project as MP3</strong><br />Go to <strong>Export</strong> and export the project.<br />

<img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/34478880525201" alt="" />

<br />

<em>
  Note: This step is required for updating Audio Native, even if you don't need the MP3 file.
</em>

<strong>Publish the updated version</strong><br />Once the MP3 export is complete, go to <strong>Export > Publish > Audio Native</strong>.

<strong>Select the updated version</strong><br />Click <strong>Published version</strong> and select the newly exported version of your audio to update the embedded player.<br />

<img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/34478870511121" alt="" />

Your Audio Native player will now reflect the latest version of your project.

 

### <strong>Updating the Player Title and Author</strong>

To change the title or author shown in the Audio Native player:

* Go to the corresponding Studio project editor

* Click the hamburger menu (☰) and select Project Settings<br />

  <img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/34478870512913" alt="" />

* Go to the Export tab<br />

  <img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/34478870513681" alt="" />

* Edit the Title and Author fields<br />
  <img src="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/article_attachments/34478880531601" alt="" />

These changes will be reflected automatically in the embedded player.

# Are there any limits on the types of content I can listen to in ElevenReader?

# Are there any limits on the types of content I can listen to in ElevenReader?

Yes, content uploaded to ElevenReader for listening is governed by the <a href="https://elevenlabs.io/use-policy">ElevenLabs Prohibited Use Policy</a>. This policy supplements our Terms of Service and applies to your access and use of our services, and is intended to ensure ElevenLabs’ services are not used for illicit purposes.

We use a combination of automated systems, user reports, and human review to assess material and usage that may violate this Policy. For users who violate this Policy, we may remove the violating material, and/or suspend your access to and use of our Services.

Some specific examples of content that may violate this policy include:

Do not threaten child safety.

Do not engage in illegal behavior.

Do not create violent, hateful, or harassing material outside of fictional contexts.

If you believe your account has been incorrectly banned, or your material has been incorrectly removed, you can let us know by emailing [team@elevenlabs.io](mailto:team@elevenlabs.io) from the email you currently use for your ElevenLabs account.

# How do ElevenReader hours work?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader/how-do-eleven-reader-hours-work.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How do ElevenReader hours work?

<strong>
  What are ElevenReader hours, and how do they work?
</strong>

ElevenReader lets you listen by converting text into hours of audio. Hours are only used when you convert your imported text into audio for the first time. 

* Hours are estimated for easy reference and are based on the amount of text converted and the speed at which you listen. The faster you listen, the quicker hours will be used in generating audio.
* Each plan's hours are based on listening at normal (1.0x) playback speed.
* You are not charged for listening to text you’ve already converted into audio and played before.
* You are not charged hours for listening to any of the thousands of free books or feeds in the Explore library.
* Additionally, Ultra subscribers gain access to 20 hours every month of premium audiobooks and ebooks from the Explore catalog.

<strong>
  Are ElevenLabs plans the same as ElevenReader plans?
</strong>

No, ElevenReader offers its own subscription plans with an hourly system designed for listening to content on-the-go. ElevenLabs plans are different from ElevenReader plans.

 

<strong>
  Are hours included in the free plan?
</strong>

Yes. The free plan includes 10 free hours per month, which resets monthly.

 

<strong>
  Can I buy hours without a subscription?
</strong>

Yes. You can purchase hours without having an active subscription with hourly packs. This allows you to convert your content into audio without committing to a recurring plan. Keep in mind that some advanced features may still require a subscription to access, even if you have hours.

 

<strong>
  If I buy a pack while on the free plan, will those be added to my two hours?
</strong>

Yes, hourly packs are additive. This means that if you buy a pack with 15 hours, for example, those will be added to your 10 hours for a total of 25 hours.

 

<strong>
  What’s the difference between buying hours and subscribing?
</strong>

A subscription gives you ongoing access to premium features for a set period (monthly or yearly), while purchasing hours is a separate form of usage-based access for listening. Depending on your plan, you will receive a set number of hours each month, or you can purchase additional hours separately.

 

<strong>
  Do hours expire?
</strong>

Yes. Free plans get 10 hours that expire and reset each month. Purchased hours expire 12 months after being issued for both subscriptions and one-time packs. ElevenReader uses your subscription hours first, then any extra hours you've purchased — so you get the most listening time possible.

 

<strong>
  Will I get hours for referring a friend?
</strong>

Yes. If you refer a friend and they join through your link, both of you will earn hours upon your friend’s successful sign-up. The amount of hours you’ll earn is listed in the app.

# How can I create my own voices in ElevenReader?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader/how-can-i-create-my-own-voices-in-eleven-reader.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How can I create my own voices in ElevenReader?

ElevenReader’s Voice Design lets you create your own narrator voices with a simple text prompt.

For example,<em>“A woman in her late 20s to early 30s with a soft, airy, breathy timbre. Neutral American accent. Very slow, intimate pacing, low volume, close-mic’d delivery that feels personal and confidential. Gentle emotional warmth. Studio-quality audio with subtle intimacy.”</em>

This feature is included for ElevenReader Ultra subscribers. You can create unlimited voices and easily delete those you no longer use. If you cancel your subscription, you will no longer have access to voices created with Voice Design and you will not be able to create new voices. 

A well-crafted prompt can be the difference between a generic voice and one that truly fits your vision. In general, more descriptive and granular prompts tend to yield more accurate and nuanced results. The more detail you provide — including age, gender, tone, accent, pacing, emotion, style, and more - the better the model can interpret and deliver a voice that feels intentional and tailored. 

For more tips on writing effective prompts, see our <a href="/docs/eleven-creative/voices/voice-design#prompting-guide">Voice Design prompting guide</a>.

# How do I cancel my ElevenReader subscription?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader/how-do-i-cancel-my-eleven-reader-subscription.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How do I cancel my ElevenReader subscription?

You can cancel your subscription anytime through the platform where you subscribed:

<strong>Apple users</strong>: Go to Settings > \[your name] > Subscriptions.

<strong>Google Play users</strong>: Open the Play Store > tap your profile icon > Payments &
subscriptions > Subscriptions.

<strong>Website users</strong>: Click on your Avatar to access Account details > Manage billing.

Cancelling will prevent future charges, but you'll still have access until the end of your current billing period.

 

<strong>
  I paid for a year, can I downgrade to monthly halfway through?
</strong>

Subscriptions cannot be downgraded mid-cycle through app stores. Once your current annual plan ends, you can choose a monthly option when resubscribing.

 

<strong>
  Can I pause my subscription instead of cancelling?
</strong>

At this time, we don’t offer the option to pause a subscription. If you no longer wish to be charged, we recommend cancelling your current plan. You’ll continue to have access to premium features until the end of your current billing cycle, and you can resubscribe at any time.

 

<strong>
  What happens to my files/books if I cancel my subscription?
</strong>

When you cancel your subscription, you will retain access to your files or books used during your subscription period. However, access to premium features – such as offline mode – will be restricted once the subscription ends.

 

<strong>
  What happens to my hours if I cancel my subscription/downgrade to the free plan?
</strong>

If you cancel your subscription, any unused hours from that plan will remain in your account for up to 12 months — but you won’t be able to use them while on the free plan. To use those hours again, you’ll need to reactivate a paid subscription at any time within the 12-month expiration window. When you downgrade, you’ll lose access to paid features like offline downloads and extended listening hours. <br />

# How do I troubleshoot my ElevenReader Ultra promotion activation or redemption?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader/how-do-i-troubleshoot-my-eleven-reader-ultra-promotion-activation-or-redemption.md

# How do I troubleshoot my ElevenReader Ultra promotion activation or redemption?

ElevenReader Ultra is available through promotional partnerships with a range of partners, including telecom providers, banks, and others.

To redeem your offer:

Use the direct link provided within your partner's app or loyalty program.

Ensure you do not have an active ElevenReader Ultra subscription, if you do, you will need to
wait until it expires before redeeming a promotional subscription.

If the partner's app crashes or the connection is lost during sign-up, return to the partner's
app or loyalty program and try again.

If the page keeps loading or displays a blank screen, clear your browser's cache and cookies, or
the app's cache, and try again. Also disable any active VPN, as VPNs can interfere with
location-based voucher verification and cause failures. If the issue is with the partner's app
itself, contact their support team directly.

Each promotional code can only be redeemed once.

To confirm your subscription is active, open the ElevenReader app, tap the profile icon on the
Home screen, and check that your account displays "Ultra" status.

If you're still experiencing issues after redeeming your offer, contact ElevenReader support using this <a href="https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/en-us/requests/new">form</a>.

# How does the ElevenReader Chrome extension work?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader/how-does-the-eleven-reader-chrome-extension-work.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How does the ElevenReader Chrome extension work?

The ElevenReader Chrome extension makes it easy to import and listen to online content directly in ElevenReader. Once signed in, you can instantly import articles, web pages, or stories without copying links or switching tabs. The extension also supports capturing paywalled or complex pages, auto-importing ePUB files, detecting downloaded documents, highlighting text for quick import, and combining multiple chapters into a single continuous read.

 

<strong>
  How do I install and sign in?
</strong>

First, install the [Chrome extension](https://elevenreader.io/text-to-speech-chrome-extension) from the [Google Chrome Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/elevenreader-%E2%80%94-text-reade/mahgnmmldchnmmdfkfcoindpgkadhhhc). The extension automatically recognizes your logged-in ElevenReader account. If you’re not signed in, you’ll be prompted to log in before importing content.

<strong>
  How do I import content?
</strong>

Click the ElevenReader extension icon in your browser to import the content of the current web page.

The extension captures the full HTML content of the page, even if the material is behind a paywall once you’re logged in.

Once imported, select <strong>Listen Now</strong> to open and play the content directly on<a href="https://elevenreader.io"> elevenreader.io</a>.

<strong>
  How do I import files?
</strong>

The extension detects supported file types (ePUB, PDF, TXT) as they’re downloaded.

* ePUBs can be imported automatically.
* PDFs and TXT files will prompt you before import.
* You can adjust these preferences in the extension’s settings.<br />

<strong>
  Highlighted text
</strong>

When you highlight more than 1,000 characters on a webpage, the extension will prompt you to import that section directly into ElevenReader.

<strong>
  Bulk chapter import
</strong>

If a “Next Chapter” link is detected on your current webpage, the extension will display an <strong>Add Next Chapter</strong> button. Clicking this option collects all subsequent chapters and merges them into a single continuous read. This is best for web novels, fan fiction, and other chapter-based online reading. 

<strong>
  Troubleshooting
</strong>

If the extension doesn’t appear to import content correctly:

* Make sure you’re signed in to your ElevenReader account.
* Try refreshing the page and clicking the extension again.
* Check that your browser has permission to access downloaded files.
* Restart Chrome if imports remain incomplete.
* Uninstall and re-install the Chrome extension. <br />

If the problem persists,[ ](https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=13145996177937)please email us at [team@elevenlabs.io](mailto:team@elevenlabs.io) and include a short description of what’s happening so we can help.

# How does the Ultra plan work?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader/how-does-the-ultra-plan-work.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How does the Ultra plan work?

The Ultra plan includes up to 24 hours of audio per day for your own imported content (PDFs, text, links, ePubs, docs, and more) at normal (1.0x) speed. Listening to your text-to-audio for your files at a higher playback speed will consume these hours at a faster rate.  

Plus, Ultra subscribers gain access to 20 hours per month of premium audiobooks and ebooks from our Explore catalog. The plan cannot be shared with other accounts. 

The Ultra plan also includes:

* Offline downloads, allowing you to save your imported content or premium audiobooks in advance of being without an internet connection
* Custom voices, which let you design your own narrator voice for your text-to-audio or where selecting a voice is available

You can find all the Ultra features on our <a href="https://elevenreader.io/pricing">ElevenReader pricing page</a>.

# How do offline downloads work?

# How do offline downloads work?

Offline Downloads let you convert text into audio ahead of time, so you can listen without an internet connection. You can use them to save articles, PDFs, ebooks, and other content for offline listening.<br /><br />With the updated experience, you can choose to download specific sections of your content (such as individual chapters) or the entire text for offline use.<br /><br /><strong>How many Offline Download hours do I get?</strong><br /><br />Paid subscribers receive up to <strong>20 hours of Offline Downloads per day</strong>. If you need more, you can purchase additional <strong>one-time Offline Download hours</strong> to convert more text into audio.<br /><br /><strong>How long does it take to create an Offline Download?</strong><br /><br />Creating an Offline Download typically takes <strong>2–5 minutes</strong>, though larger files may take longer to process.<br /><br /><strong>How do I use my Offline Downloads?</strong><br /><br />Once ready, your downloads are stored directly in the app and can be played anytime — even without Wi-Fi or mobile data. You can remove downloads at any time to free up device storage and are removed when you sign out.<br /><br />For larger files, you may be asked to select specific chapters or sections to download rather than downloading the entire file at once.<br /><br /><strong>Do Offline Downloads expire?</strong><br /><br />Yes. Offline Downloads remain available for <strong>60 days</strong> after they are created. You’ll receive a notification <strong>7 days before expiration</strong>, giving you time to renew the download if needed.

# If I uninstall the ElevenReader app, will I still be charged?

# Is content between ElevenReader and the website shared?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader/is-content-between-eleven-reader-and-the-website-shared.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# Is content between ElevenReader and the website shared?

Yes. All your files in ElevenReader on iOS and Android sync with your ElevenReader account on web/desktop ([elevenreader.io](https://elevenreader.io/)). You can log in on any device to view and listen to your files. Some features may not yet be fully available on web.

Your ElevenReader ([elevenreader.io](https://elevenreader.io/)) account is separate from an E[l](https://elevenlabs.io/)evenLabs ([elevenlabs.io](https://elevenlabs.io/)) account.

# What is ElevenReader?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader/what-is-eleven-reader.md

# What is ElevenReader?

ElevenReader is a powerful tool that enables users to convert text into natural, expressive speech. Whether you're reading articles, EPUBs, PDFs, or any form of text, this app is designed to enhance your reading experience by providing high-quality, human-like voices in 32 languages.

Leveraging ElevenLabs' most advanced Text to Speech (TTS) model, ElevenReader places the cutting-edge technology of ElevenLabs right in your pocket.

  Download for iOS (iPhone and iPad)
</a>

# Which devices is ElevenReader available on?

ElevenReader is available in countries and on devices where supported, and supports 32 languages.

* Sign up or sign in for web at [elevenreader.io](https://elevenreader.io/)

Phones with unlocked bootloader and rooted devices are not supported due to security measures.

# What is the maximum file length supported in ElevenReader?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader/what-is-the-maximum-file-length-supported-in-eleven-reader.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# What is the maximum file length supported in ElevenReader?

ElevenReader currently supports uploads of files up to 500 pages.

If your document exceeds 500 pages, you’ll need to split it into smaller parts before uploading. Once divided into separate files under the page limit, they can be uploaded and read normally within the app.

This limit applies to large document uploads to ensure stable parsing and playback performance.

# Which voices can I use in ElevenReader?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader/which-voices-can-i-use-in-eleven-reader.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# Which voices can I use in ElevenReader?

The app features hundreds of curated, quality voices produced with ElevenLabs, including our Iconic Voices collection. 

We provide recommended voices based on your language settings, and you can create your own voices from a text prompt using Voice Design within the app. ElevenReader does not support voices you've created yourself using voice cloning. 

Additionally, the app features thousands of audiobooks with human-narrated, premium audiobooks. For select titles, you may be able to select your own narrator where listed on the book’s listing page.

# Can I pre-select my preferred voice narration for my book?

No, at this time you cannot pre-select an AI voice narration for your book. Each user will have the option to choose their own AI voice narration from the voice library. If you would like to recommend a voice, we suggest adding a text note at the beginning of your book. For example: <em>“The author recommends listening to this book using the voice Lily.”</em>

# Are there situations where my payments might be delayed or withheld?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/are-there-situations-where-my-payments-might-be-delayed-or-withheld.md

# Are there situations where my payments might be delayed or withheld?

Yes, payments can be delayed or withheld if there’s a violation of the [Terms](https://elevenreader.io/publishing-terms-of-service), invalid activity, like artificial downloads or suspicious actions, is detected, or when payments are under investigation for any other reason. If no violations are found, payments will resume.

# How are payouts calculated?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/how-are-payouts-calculated.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How are payouts calculated?

<strong>
  Direct Sales
</strong>

For direct purchases, ElevenReader Publishing pays authors <strong>60% of the revenue collected</strong>, after deducting store fees, in accordance with our standard publishing agreement.

* Apple App Store and Google Play Store fees are typically <strong>30%</strong> of the in-app purchase price
* Web purchases are subject to an approximately <strong>3% Stripe processing fee</strong>
* Tax withholdings may apply depending on your country of residence

<strong>
  Subscription Listening
</strong>

For books included in the Ultra subscription, authors earn <strong>$0.20 per hour of verified listening streamed, with a cap of $2.50 per book</strong>.

# How can I delete/unlist a book that has been published?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/how-can-i-delete-unlist-a-book-that-has-been-published.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How can I delete/unlist a book that has been published?

To delete or unlist a book that has been published on the ElevenReader app, navigate to [ElevenReader.io](https://elevenreader.io/), open the 'Bookshelf' tab, and locate the book you wish to unlist. Click 'View Details' to open the book detail tab, where you will find various options. Select 'Unlist' to remove your book from the ElevenReader app content library.

Once unlisted, your book will no longer be visible to new users.

# How can I preview and listen to my book in audio on the ElevenReader app?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/how-can-i-preview-and-listen-to-my-book-in-audio-on-the-eleven-reader-app.md

# How can I preview and listen to my book in audio on the ElevenReader app?

To preview and listen to your book in audio on the ElevenReader App, navigate to <strong>‘Preview audio in ElevenReader app’</strong> in the top-right menu bar of the publishing editor and click it. This will open a pop-up that generates a unique QR code for your book, which you can scan with your phone’s camera (note: scan with your camera application, not via the ElevenReader app). Your phone will then open the ElevenReader app (please ensure you have the latest version installed) and display your book preview in-app.

You can select a voice and play the audio, converting your book into an audiobook. This is how your book will appear to readers in the app. If you need to make any edits to the text, return to the publishing editor, make the changes, and generate a new QR code that will lead you to the updated version of your book. Continue to edit your book  until you are satisfied with the preview. Now you can proceed to <strong>‘Prepare for publishing’</strong> to add additional information about your book.

# How do I earn money from my books on ElevenReader?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/how-do-i-earn-money-from-my-books-on-eleven-reader.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How do I earn money from my books on ElevenReader?

There are <strong>two ways to earn from your books on ElevenReader</strong>

1. Engagement-Based Payouts (Ultra Subscription)

ElevenReader Ultra subscribers receive <strong>20 hours of listening</strong> bundled into their subscription.

* Books included in the Ultra subscription earn <strong>$0.20 per hour of verified listening streamed, with a cap of $2.50 per book.</strong>
* Listening is calculated based on validated playback
* Earnings accrue as subscribers engage with your content

This model rewards high quality content and sustained engagement. 

2. Direct Sales

You can list your books for <strong>direct purchase</strong> and choose how they’re made available:

* <strong>
    Direct sale to all users (Free & Ultra)
  </strong>
  <br />
  All ElevenReader users purchase your book outright, and you earn a 60% revenue share on each sale.
* <strong>
    Hybrid: Subscription + Direct Sale
  </strong>
  <br />
  Your book is bundled into the Ultra subscription for subscribers (earning engagement-based
  payouts), while free users can purchase the book directly. Simply opt-in to the subscription,
  while also setting a direct sale price to enable this option.

This flexibility allows you to balance reach, engagement, and upfront sales.

# How can I share my book with my audience?

Once your book has been reviewed and approved (status changes to ‘Published’), the sharing option becomes available. To share your book with readers, family and friends, follow these steps from [https://elevenreader.io/app/publishing](https://elevenreader.io/app/publishing) 

**From the ‘Bookshelf’ View:**

* Navigate to the main ‘Bookshelf’ view and locate the book you want to share.
* A right-pointing arrow will be visible; click it to open the ‘Share Your Book’ pop-up.
* Choose one of the sharing options displayed QR code or link
* The unique sharing link directs users to a web-based preview of your book, where they can add it to their ElevenReader library or listen to a preview.
* Example: [ElevenReader Book Preview](https://elevenreader.io/app/reader/audiobooks/80FhHw9UAvL81UlroNT4)

**From the ‘View Details’ Page:**

* Navigate to the main ‘Bookshelf’ view and locate the book you want to share.
* Click ‘View Details’ to open the book details page.
* At the bottom, you will find options to ‘Unlist,’ ‘Share,’ or ‘View Reports.’
* Click ‘Share’ and copy the unique qr code or sharing link from there.

This sharing feature allows you to promote your book easily, ensuring readers can discover and engage with your content on the ElevenReader app. Please note that readers must have the app installed to access the book in full.

# What information is included in ElevenReader Publishing reports?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/what-information-is-included-in-eleven-reader-publishing-reports.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# What information is included in ElevenReader Publishing reports?

The ElevenReader Publishing program will provide you with detailed insights into how users interact with your content. In the ‘Reports’ tab on the publishing main page, you will find real-time charts that allow you to track engagement with you content from ElevenReader App content. Reports also include payout information. 

Below is a list of definitions to help you navigate. Note that the top tiles in your report represent lifetime statistics, while you can set a preferred date range by selecting a custom date, last 30 days, or last 90 days. This can be applied to all titles or selected ones via the dropdown menu.

* Total Users: The number of users who have added your book to their personal libraries on the ElevenReader app.
* Total Payouts: The total amount of payouts received from published content.
* Total Listening Duration: The total amount of time users have spent listening to your content on a given day in hours and minutes.
* Listener Engagement: The number of users progressing through your book at 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% completion.
* Ratings: Star ratings users have given your book on a scale from 1 to 5, along with the count of each rating.
* Average Rating: The average star rating from all users.
* Top Voices: The most frequently used voices for listening to your book.

We aim to add more analytics soon, let us know what insights you're interested in!

# What do I need to look out for in the publishing editor?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/what-do-i-need-to-look-out-for-in-the-publishing-editor.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# What do I need to look out for in the publishing editor?

When uploading a manuscript to the publishing editor, it will automatically process the file for you, splitting it into multiple chapters. In the publishing editor, you can make text-based edits, add, delete, or rearrange chapters, and reformat headers. Note that not all formatting from the original manuscript will be retained to ensure compatibility with AI audio narration. We recommend reviewing the following to create a great reading and audio experience for your readers on the ElevenReader app:

* Ensure the manuscript is complete and that all chapters have been transferred to the publishing editor. If there are significant differences from the original manuscript, consider uploading a different file type or restarting the publishing editor to manually copy over the manuscript.
* The first chapter or page view should include the book title and author information.
* The table of contents can be deleted, as the reader can navigate through chapters directly within the ElevenReader app.
* Chapter titles should be formatted using Heading 1–3 for better organization.
* Detailed information that doesn’t translate well into audio can be moved to the back of the book.
* Validate that the text doesn’t contain page references or unwanted artifacts, which can be removed directly in the editor.
* Remove any unnecessary blank spaces in the text for a cleaner presentation.

These steps help ensure an optimal reading and listening experience for your audience on the ElevenReader app.

# What is ElevenLabs and the ElevenReader App?

ElevenLabs is an Audio AI research and deployment company. Our mission is to make content universally accessible in any language and in any voice. Our research team develops advanced AI audio models that generate realistic, versatile and contextually-aware speech, sound effects, and voices across 32 languages. Access the ElevenLabs platform here: [https://elevenlabs.io](https://elevenlabs.io)

ElevenReader is a text-to-audio and audiobook app for iOS, Android, and web. It is widely available in countries and on devices where supported in 32 languages. Choose from 200,000+ premium audiobooks and eBooks — or bring your own content. Upload any PDF, article, EPUB, or document and hear it in stunningly natural voices you choose from a library of 1,000+ options across languages. Download free from the App Store or Google Play, or get started on the web at [ElevenReader.io](http://ElevenReader.io).

* [Download for iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/elevenreader-text-to-speech/id6479373050?platform=iphone) - Requires iOS 17.0 or later.
* [Download for iPad](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/elevenreader-text-to-speech/id6479373050?platform=ipad) - Requires iPadOS 17.0 or later.
* [Download for Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.elevenlabs.readerapp\&pli=1) - Requires Android 7.0 or later.
* Sign up or sign in for web at [elevenreader.io](https://elevenreader.io/)

# What is the difference between revenue and earnings?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/what-is-the-difference-between-revenue-and-earnings.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# What is the difference between revenue and earnings?

<strong>Revenue</strong> is the gross amount generated from book sales on ElevenReader before any
fees, royalties, or taxes.

<br />

<strong>Earnings</strong> are the amount you receive in your payout after all applicable fees,
royalties, and taxes are deducted.

# What is the difference between AI audio narration and AI audiobook production?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/what-is-the-difference-between-ai-audio-narration-and-ai-audiobook-production.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# What is the difference between AI audio narration and AI audiobook production?

* <strong>AI audio narration:</strong> On-demand audio generation; users select voices; no upfront
  production or editing required.
* <strong>AI audiobook production:</strong> Audio production in a full-control text and audio
  editing environment. This provides a high-degree of creative control, as each producer selects
  voice(s) and quality controls for text-to-speech output.

# What was the introductory payment program and does it apply to my books?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/what-was-the-introductory-payment-program-and-does-it-apply-to-my-books.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# What was the introductory payment program and does it apply to my books?

Our introductory program was a beta offering designed as a limited-time promotional rate while we built and tested the platform. We're currently transitioning all authors from our introductory beta program to a new engagement-based payout model.

If you're enrolled in engagement-based payouts, here's what applies to you:

* Now through February 19, 2026: All authors currently earn under the introductory program terms (\$1.10 per engaged listener), regardless of when you joined
* February 19, 2026 onward: All authors enrolled in engagement based payouts will automatically transition to the new payout model ($0.20 per hour of verified listening, with a $2.50 cap per book)

Note: If you joined recently, you agreed to the new payout terms during enrollment. However, as we transition, the introductory program rates will apply until February 15, 2026.

No action needed. This transition happens automatically for all enrolled authors.

# When will I get paid?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/eleven-reader-publishing/when-will-i-get-paid.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# When will I get paid?

Unique engaged users are recorded consistently, whilst payments are made every two weeks. However, you must reach a minimum earnings threshold of \$10 (USD) before payments are sent. If you don’t meet this threshold, your earnings will roll over to the next payment cycle.

# How do I use GenFM?

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/distribution-publishing/gen-fm/how-do-i-use-gen-fm.md

> This is a page from the ElevenLabs documentation. For a complete page index, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms.txt. For the full documentation in a single file, fetch https://elevenlabs.io/docs/llms-full.txt.

# How do I use GenFM?

GenFM is available in [Studio](https://elevenlabs.io/app/studio). It allows you to automatically create a podcast based on any document you provide.

<strong>
  Studio
</strong>

Go to [Studio](https://elevenlabs.io/app/projects), and under <strong>Get started</strong>, choose <strong>Generate audio</strong>. Select <strong>Generate a podcast</strong> from the available options, and you can then select options for your podcast.

For the source material for your podcast, you can upload a document (EPUB, PDF, TXT, or HTML), provide a URL, or link to an existing project. Either use the suggested voice pairing or choose any voice from My Voices for the Host and Guest. Choose your model and quality setting, then click <strong>Generate</strong>, and the text for your podcast will be generated.

You can check and edit the text of your podcast before you convert it to audio. When you're happy, click <strong>Convert</strong> and the audio will be generated. Once that's done, you will be able to download the audio and listen to your new podcast. 

If you already have a script ready, we recommend starting with either <strong>New empty audio project</strong> or <strong>Narrate an audiobook,</strong> as using GenFM via the <strong>Generate a podcast</strong> option will modify your script.

# Managing Your ElevenLabs Subscription (Mobile App vs. Website)

**URL:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/mobile-apps/eleven-labs-for-ios-and-android/managing-your-eleven-labs-subscription-mobile-app-vs-website.md
